correctness.rationale: PASS: For every gamma,c>0, the Jacobi theta_4 product is positive and its logarithmic elasticity Phi(u)=uS'(u)/S(u) is a continuous strictly decreasing map (0,infinity) onto (0,infinity). Each product summand mu/(exp(mu)-1) strictly decreases; Poisson summation gives Phi(u)~pi^2/(4u)-1/2 at zero, while exponential tails give zero at infinity. With u=gamma/b^2 and b^2=gamma/u, the alternating bounded pre-Gramian vector cancels odd rows by k<->j-k and even rows because cb^2 S-S'=0. Lemvig Proposition 2.1 for M^1 windows then establishes an actual nonframe on ab=1/2. Direct log-curvature g gives strong log-concavity iff gamma c>1, strict log-concavity at equality, and two maxima below; theta asymptotics derive both stated scale laws. Independent bounded calculations sampled four (gamma,c) choices and 17 rows per case and theta monotonicity; infinite proof rests on product/Poisson/parity, not these checks.
